name: bearings
title: Bearings
tagline: Map points joined by paths with north lines and clockwise three-figure bearing arcs; bearings and back bearings derived from positions, always to scale.
description: A bearings diagram: named points on a map plane (north is up), joined by straight paths (journey legs or sight lines), with a north line at the measured points and a bearing arc swept clockwise from north round to a path, labelled with its three-figure bearing (000°–359°). You place the points — by absolute map coordinates, or by a bearing-and-distance leg from another point — and choose which bearings to mark; the bearing angle and the back (reverse) bearing are derived from the positions, so the figure is always to scale and a marked value can never lie. Per-bearing occlusion ("measure the bearing", shown as "?"), highlighting the answer, an optional compass rose for compass-point work, authored distance labels on legs, a caption, and draggable points on the web (every bearing recomputes live). Covers measuring and drawing bearings, back bearings, from/to bearings, compass points, and multi-leg journeys.
whenToUse: Reach for this for anything taught with a three-figure bearing: measuring or drawing the bearing of one point from another, back (reverse) bearings, the bearing from one place to another, compass points as bearings (045° = NE), and multi-leg journeys with a bearing at each turn. Build the figure by listing points: give the first an absolute position with at [x, y] (x east, y north/up, e.g. [0, 0]), then add each further point with polar — a bearing and distance from an existing point, phrased exactly as the question is ("B is 8 km from A on a bearing of 070°" → polar: { from: "A", bearing: 70, distance: 8 }). Draw the legs/sight lines with paths (from → to, optional arrow for a journey, optional distance label), and mark a bearing with bearings: { at, to } — the protractor sits at "at", points to "to", and the value is the derived bearing of "to" from "at". A back bearing is simply { at: "B", to: "A" } (it comes out at the forward bearing ± 180°, drawn as a reflex arc when over 180°). Common configurations: measure / work out the bearing — mark the bearing and set occlude: true so it shows "?", with the question in the block text; draw a bearing — give the point its polar bearing and show the arc (occlude false); back bearing — mark both { at: A, to: B } and { at: B, to: A }; journey — two polar legs and a bearing at each turn, occluding the one you ask for; compass points — add compass: { at, eightPoint: true } for an 8-point rose. A north line is drawn automatically wherever a bearing is marked; set a point's north: true to force one elsewhere (e.g. an answer space where pupils measure for themselves). Highlight the bearing that is the answer. Cross-block convention: keep the same points and distances across the blocks of one lesson so pupils track one journey — change only which bearings are shown, occluded or highlighted. A staged build reads well: start from the labelled points and north line, add one leg and its bearing per stage. UNITS — set unit: "km" once per figure and any bare-number leg label ("8") reads "8 km"; a label carrying its own text ("8 km", "x") stays verbatim; bearings are angles and never take it. Synonyms a teacher might use: bearing, bearings, three-figure bearing, 3-figure bearing, back bearing, reverse bearing, bearing of, bearing from, compass bearing, true bearing, due north/east/south/west, compass points, north-east, NE, journey, navigation, scale drawing, map. @3 — ANSWER ON THE MODEL: for a "mark the position of C with a cross" question give placePoint and host the tile with responseMode "place-point" and marking.correctAnswer { derived: true }. Use { from, bearing, distance } for "C is <distance> from A on a bearing of <b>°" (the pupil drags a cross; the model marks the bearing within angleTol and the distance within distanceTol — the mark-scheme band); use { intersect: [{ from, bearing }, { from, bearing }] } for "C is on a bearing of X from A and Y from B" (marked within posTol of the crossing). The target is never drawn on the posed figure — the answer space is a padded blank — so the completed plot belongs in the worked-solution figure (a normal point C, or ctx.reveal). @3 — RIGHT-ANGLE MARK: add rightAngles: [{ at, to }] to draw the 90° square between the north line and a due-E/W leg where the bearing is read off the right angle (e.g. A due west of P ⇒ the bearing of A from P is 270°).

points.description: The named points (places) in the figure. Each carries a position — given EITHER absolutely with at, OR relatively with polar (a bearing+distance from another point). The first point is usually absolute; later points build off it. Positions are the only authored geometry; every bearing is derived from them.

id.description: Short identifier used to reference this point in paths, bearings and compass (e.g. "A", "B", "Port"). Must be unique. Also the default display label.

at.description: Absolute map coordinates [x, y]: x measured EAST, y measured NORTH (up). Use for the first / reference point, e.g. [0, 0]. Provide at OR polar, not both.

polar.description: Place this point relative to another by a bearing-and-distance leg — phrase it exactly as the question does. The bearing of this point FROM `from` then derives back to this same value, so it can be marked and occluded as a question without ever lying. Provide polar OR at, not both.

from.description: id of the point this one is measured from (must be another point in the list).

bearing.description: Bearing of this point from `from`, in degrees clockwise from north (0–360). 70 places it on a bearing of 070°.

distance.description: Map distance from `from` (same units across the figure — keep distances proportional to the real ones so the drawing is to scale). Default 5 when omitted (for figures where only the direction matters).

label.description: Display name drawn beside the point. Defaults to id. Set it to show a fuller name (e.g. "Harbour") while keeping a short id for references.

north.description: Force a north line at this point even when no bearing is marked here — e.g. an answer space where pupils measure the bearing themselves. A north line is drawn automatically at any point that is a bearing vertex, so this is only needed elsewhere. Default false.

paths.description: The straight lines drawn between points — journey legs or sight lines. A bearing marked between two points already draws its own sight line, so list a path here for legs you want drawn in their own right (a journey, the return leg, a triangle side), to add a distance label, or to make a leg a directed arrow.

label.description: Text along the leg, typically a distance ("8 km"). Authored — the model does not compute real-world lengths. A bare-number label ("8") takes the figure's `unit` automatically ("8 km"); a label with any other text ("8 km", "x") is shown verbatim. Omit for an unlabelled line.

arrow.description: Draw a direction arrowhead at the `to` end — use for a directed journey leg. Default false (a plain sight line).

style.description: "solid" (default) for a travelled leg / sight line; "dashed" for a construction or return reference line.

bearings.description: The bearings to MARK with a north line, a clockwise arc and a three-figure value. Each is the bearing of `to` FROM `at`: the protractor sits at `at` (where the north line is) and points to `to`. The value is DERIVED from the positions and stays correct under drag; a sweep over 180° draws as a reflex arc. A back bearing is just { at: B, to: A }.

at.description: id of the point the bearing is measured AT (the north line / protractor sits here).

to.description: id of the point the bearing is measured TO. The arc sweeps clockwise from north round to the direction of this point.

occlude.description: Render the value as "?" — the "measure / work out the bearing" hook. The north line and arc still show. Default false.

highlight.description: Draw the eye to this bearing (amber arc + value) — the answer, or the bearing a question is about. Default false.

label.description: Override the displayed value — for a known/algebraic value only ("x", "2x"). Omit to show the derived three-figure bearing; the arc is always drawn true to the geometry regardless.

compass.description: Draw a compass rose centred on a point — the teaching aid for compass-point work (045° = NE). Omit for no rose.

at.description: id of the point to centre the rose on.

eightPoint.description: Show the eight points (N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW). Default false shows the four cardinal points (N, E, S, W) only.

northLabels.description: Label each north line "N". Default true.

grid.description: Show a faint background square grid (helps read a scale drawing). Default false — most bearings figures are gridless.

header.description: Optional short title centred above the figure; the top padding grows to clear it.

caption.description: Optional line centred below the figure, e.g. the fact being taught. Never the question or an instruction: that wording is the block's text.

draggable.description: Web-only. Let pupils drag a point to reposition it; every bearing, back bearing and arc recomputes live, staying true to the new positions. Snaps to the grid of map units. Default false.

unit.description: The figure's distance unit, e.g. "km", "m", "mi". Appended to every path-leg distance label (paths[].label) that is a BARE NUMBER ("8" → "8 km"). A label with any other text ("8 km", "x") is shown verbatim — an authored override always wins. Bearings (angles) never take it. Default "" (labels stay bare). Set it once per figure and keep it consistent across a lesson. @2.

rightAngles.description: Right-angle square marks (@3): each { at, to } draws the 90° square in the corner between the north line at `at` and the leg to `to`. LOAD-BEARING where a point is due east/west of another — the bearing is then read off the right angle (A due west of P ⇒ the bearing of A from P is 270°). The author asserts the perpendicularity, so place it only where the geometry is a true 90°. Structural neutral, like the north line it corners against.

at.description: id of the vertex the square sits at (has a north line — a bearing vertex, or north: true).

to.description: id of the point the perpendicular leg runs to.

placePoint.description: Answer-on-the-model target (@3) for a marked place-point response — host the tile with responseMode "place-point" and marking.correctAnswer { derived: true }. The point the pupil must PLOT with a cross. It is DERIVED and NEVER drawn on the posed figure (print / slide pose only a padded blank answer space); the model self-checks the placed cross against the mark-scheme band in its own closure, so no coordinate reaches the DOM. Give EXACTLY ONE target shape: a polar leg (from + bearing + distance), the crossing of two bearings (intersect), or an absolute point (at). Phrase it exactly as the question does ("2.5 km from A on a bearing of 210°" → { from: "A", bearing: 210, distance: 2.5 }).

from.description: Polar target: id of the anchor the point is measured from. The placed cross is checked as the bearing-and-distance of that cross from `from`.

bearing.description: Polar target: the bearing of the point from `from`, degrees clockwise from north.

distance.description: Polar target: the distance from `from`, in the figure's map units. Public — it IS the question — and it sizes the answer space, but the position is never drawn.

intersect.description: Intersect target: the CROSSING of two bearing rays — [{ from, bearing }, { from, bearing }]. Use for "C is on a bearing of X from A and Y from B; mark C". The pupil sees a sight line from each anchor as they place the cross.

from.description: id of the anchor this bearing ray starts from.

bearing.description: Bearing of the ray from `from`, degrees clockwise from north.

at.description: Absolute target [x, y] (east, north) — an escape hatch for a fixed answer. Prefer polar/intersect so the target reads straight from the question and reveals nothing.

label.description: Label drawn beside the plotted cross and the revealed target. Default "C".

angleTol.description: Polar target: bearing tolerance in degrees (the mark-scheme band). Default 2.

distanceTol.description: Polar target: distance tolerance in map units. Default 0.3.

posTol.description: Intersect / absolute target: radial tolerance in map units around the derived point. Default 0.4.

reach.description: Override the auto answer-space radius reserved around the anchor(s), in map units. Default: polar 1.3×distance; intersect 0.6×anchor separation. Raise it if the target would fall off-canvas.
